NUZZLE.scope: The five units in appliesTo declare NUZZLE in this production reference. The strategy is shared; the unit-specific differences are only the star count (table index), the passive and the stats. Pachirisu's own passive (Passive.PACHIRISU) is NOT covered here (see passiveGaps).
NUZZLE.summary: Moves the caster to a free cell next to an enemy chosen by Board.getFarthestTargetCoordinateAvailablePlace (usually far from the caster, but NOT guaranteed to be the farthest enemy: see targeting), retargets to that enemy, then paralyses it and deals special damage. If the helper returns null the caster stays and hits the cast target.

targeting.who: the enemy attached to the helper's selected cell: scanning enemies in board order, each enemy whose distance is STRICTLY greater than the running maximum updates the maximum and, only if it has at least one free adjacent cell, replaces the selected destination (and its enemy). The cast target is replaced by that enemy.
targeting.note: Cases (read from the helper, not executed): (1) normal: the last maximum-setting enemy that has a free adjacent cell is chosen, with the free adjacent cell farthest from the caster (first such cell on ties). (2) RETAINED SELECTION: if an enemy that sets a new maximum distance has no free adjacent cell, the earlier selectedCell is kept (it is never cleared) and its enemy - nearer than the farthest - becomes the target. (3) because the running maximum was already raised, enemies scanned later at a distance <= that maximum are skipped, even if they are nearer than the farthest enemy but farther than the retained one, and even if they have free cells. (4) FALLBACK: only if no enemy at all produced a selected cell, the free cell closest to the last-recorded 'farthest' enemy (getClosestAvailablePlace) is used with that enemy as target. (5) if that also fails (or no targettable enemy exists) the helper returns null: the caster does not move and the original cast target is hit. Ties in distance keep the first enemy in scan order (strict >). The scan order of board.forEach and the exact distanceM metric were not read.

geometry.shape: single target; caster relocates to the free adjacent cell (of the selected enemy) that is farthest from the caster, first on ties; unchanged if no cell is returned

effects.scaling: AP: damage x (1 + AP/100) (apBoost true is passed); the cast's crit flag multiplies by critPower only if the cast crit (needs ABILITY_CRIT: canCritByDefault is false)

DRAGON_RAGE.summary: Gives the caster an initial shield and starts a 6-pulse effect: each pulse (every 1000 timer units) adds more shield and hits all adjacent enemies with special damage; when the effect ends, C = min(current shield, tracked raw shield) is removed from the shield and 40 % of C (rounded) is requested as healing.

effects.condition: each pulse, to every enemy on an adjacent cell
effects.scaling: AP: x(1 + AP/100) (no apBoost argument => handleSpecialDamage default true); crit only if the cast itself crit (needs ABILITY_CRIT), and that crit flag is stored in the effect at creation
effects.resolution: then SPE_DEF division per pulse, ceil, min 1, and later modifiers

effects.condition: once on the first cast (initial) and once per pulse
effects.scaling: addShield(value, caster, apBoost 1, crit): x(1 + AP/100), x critPower if the cast crit, halved if the unit is enraged, rounded; Big Eater Belt hook in PokemonEntity.addShield
effects.resolution: the amount actually received can exceed (AP) or fall below (enrage) the raw value, while the stored counter `shieldGiven` adds the RAW value only

declaredRaw.formula: removes C shield; requests healing round(0.4 x C), where C = min(current shield, shieldGiven)
declaredRaw.note: removed shield (C) and requested healing (0.4 x C, rounded) are different amounts. shieldGiven = raw initial shield + raw per-pulse shields added since the effect (or since the last conversion) started

perUnitRaw.GYARADOS: C = 135 gives 135 shield removed and a base healing request of round(0.4 x 135) = 54 (before healing modifiers); other values of C give other amounts

effects.scaling: the healing request is not AP- or crit-scaled (handleHeal called with apBoost 0, crit false), but handleHeal then applies its own modifiers: wound => 0, burn x0.5, enraged x0.5, BUFF_HEAL_RECEIVED x1.3, zenith weather x1.2, rounding, cap at missing HP. The 54 is the BASE request, not a universal maximum: modifiers can raise or lower the healing received, and C itself varies (damage taken, recast, enrage)
effects.resolution: C depends on how much of the tracked shield is still on the unit; the removal is an exchange (shield lost) while the healing request is 40 % of it; actual healing received is whatever handleHeal returns

DRAGON_RAGE.positionalConditions: None for casting. Damage depends on which enemies are on the 8 adjacent cells at each pulse.
DRAGON_RAGE.repeatedCastsAndModes: State: a DragonRageEffect with ticksRemaining (6) and shieldGiven. FIRST cast: adds the initial shield and creates the effect. CAST WHILE ACTIVE: no new initial shield is added; the active effect converts its tracked shield into healing right away (consumeShield) and ticksRemaining is reset to 6 (the effect's 1000-unit timer is not reset). The effect ends on the pulse where ticksRemaining would go below 0, i.e. after 6 damaging pulses the 7th timer fire ends it and converts what is left. Each cast still spends maxPP of PP.
DRAGON_RAGE.rawVsResolved: Declared raw for 3 stars: initial shield 45, per pulse shield 15 and damage 15, 6 pulses; tracked raw shield 45 + 6 x 15 = 135. With C = 135 (all tracked shield still present at the end) the conversion removes 135 shield and requests round(0.4 x 135) = 54 healing as the BASE request, before handleHeal's modifiers (burn/enrage halve, wound zeroes, BUFF_HEAL_RECEIVED x1.3, zenith x1.2) and the cap at missing HP. Actual shield received includes AP scaling and may be lower after damage, so C can be smaller; it can never exceed the tracked raw counter.

DIVE.summary: Destination, self shield, relocation and adjacent burst. The strategy first computes the destination: the empty cell with the most adjacent opposing-team units (the first of the sorted list on ties; no destination is returned only if no cell is empty). Only then does it give the caster a flat shield (15/30/60/120 by stars, requested; no AP or crit scaling because apBoost 0 and crit false are passed; Big Eater Belt x1.25 and enrage x0.5 do apply). The shield is added whether or not a destination exists. If a destination exists the caster then moves there (moveTo, not a forced displacement) and deals flat SPECIAL damage (10/20/40/80 by stars, requested, with AP and crit scaling) to every enemy in the 8 cells adjacent to the new position. Without an empty cell the shield is still granted but there is no movement and no damage. requiresTarget is false, so the cast does not need a target in range.

FAKE_TEARS.label: production-branch reference; deployment unverified
FAKE_TEARS.scope: The three units in appliesTo (Gothita 1 star, Gothorita 2, Gothitelle 3) declare FAKE_TEARS; maxPP 80 and range 3 for all. Gothita and Gothorita declare passive HATCH in the catalog and Gothitelle none; HATCH is not covered here. The strategy is shared; unit differences are the star count (table index).
FAKE_TEARS.summary: Hits EVERY enemy unit on the board (every occupied cell whose unit is not on the caster's team; no range or target limit), not just the cast target. For each enemy, in board-iteration order, it first calls triggerArmorReduction(3000 ms for 1-3 stars) on that enemy and then requests SPECIAL damage (raw 5/10/15 by the caster's stars) from it. Rune Protect on an enemy's own status refuses the NEW armor-reduction application on that enemy, but that alone does not make its current armorReduction flag false: the damage step reads the flag as it is when the hit is processed. A successful application sets the flag before the damage, so the halved SPE_DEF applies to this same hit; a refused one leaves the flag as it was (false if the enemy had no earlier armor reduction, so its normal SPE_DEF applies; true if an earlier one is still flagged, because clearNegativeStatus zeroes the cooldown but not the boolean). The duration reductions (Swift Swim, Hydration, Water Veil / Surge Surfer, Odd Keystone) read the enemy that was passed as the entity argument, i.e. the TARGET of each application, not the caster. Protect, skydiving and magicBounce on an enemy are not cleared and block that enemy's damage (the armor reduction is still applied); a magicBounce enemy also queues a delayed SPECIAL bounce at the caster unless the caster holds Protective Pads.

Per enemy, handleDamage uses Math.round(speDef / 2) whenever that enemy's current armorReduction flag is true when the hit is processed (a successful application sets it just before; a Rune-Protect-refused application leaves the flag unchanged, so with no earlier flag the full SPE_DEF is used). The division is an intermediate calculation (ceil, min 1) and later untraced modifiers follow, so it is not the final HP loss; takenDamage (not used by this strategy, the return value is discarded) would count HP removed plus shield damage. An enemy with protect, skydiving or magicBounce takes 0 from the hit (the armor reduction on it is still applied first). The hit applies once per enemy, so the total across the board scales with the number of enemies.

statusEffects.applicationOrder: per enemy: armor reduction first, then that enemy's damage
statusEffects.guards: a new application is refused for an enemy whose status has runeProtect (checked on the status the method is called on, i.e. that enemy's); the refusal neither sets nor clears the flag and does not cancel that enemy's damage. A refused application (Rune Protect) does not prove the enemy's CURRENT armorReduction flag is false: the damage step reads the flag as it is when the hit is processed. triggerRuneProtect calls clearNegativeStatus, which zeroes armorReductionCooldown but not the boolean, so a flag set before Rune Protect appeared stays true until updateArmorReduction runs; with no earlier flag, a refused application leaves the normal defenses in place. When applied, the duration goes through applyStatusDurationReductions(duration, pkm) where pkm is the ENEMY itself (value, supplied as the entity argument): if that enemy has SWIFT_SWIM the duration is x0.7, else HYDRATION x0.5, else WATER_VEIL / SURGE_SURFER x0.3 (Math.round), and each Odd Keystone in that enemy's player's items takes a further 10 % off. So, unlike RAGING_BULL (which passes the caster), the reductions come from the enemy being hit and the caster's own abilities/items do not shorten it. A new application replaces the remaining time only if longer. These reductions were read in the source; the pinned helper was not executed in this run.

SLUDGE.scope: The four units in appliesTo declare SLUDGE in this production reference (all with passive NONE in the catalog, maxPP 100, range 1). The strategy is shared; differences are star count (1 or 2) and stats.
SLUDGE.summary: Applies poison to every enemy standing in the three cells directly in front of the caster (towards its target). For each such enemy the strategy makes nbStacks successive triggerPoison calls (2/3/4/8 by stars: 1 star = 2, 2 stars = 3) with a duration of 3000/3000/3000/10000 ms scaled by AP (and critPower only if the cast crit). Each call adds one stack up to a cap of 3 (4 if the caster has VENOMOUS, 5 with TOXIC). So from zero stacks and without reactions a 1-star cast requests and applies 2 stacks and a 2-star cast requests and applies 3; among the 1-3-star requests only the 3-star request (4) exceeds the base cap of 3 (it applies 3, or 4 with VENOMOUS); the declared four-star / fallback request of 8 also exceeds the base cap, but the listed units are 1- and 2-star in the catalog and no four-star availability is claimed here. The calls are not one atomic addition: immunity, Rune Protect and berry reactions are evaluated in each call (a Pecha Berry holder eats the berry during the first call, which clears the stacks and grants poison immunity, so the later calls do nothing). No direct damage. The poison then ticks about every 1000 ms: a negative computed amount requests a heal on the poisoned unit itself (reachable through the Gliscor formula), zero makes no call, a positive amount requests TRUE damage attributed to the poison origin; these are handler requests, not guaranteed HP changes.

FLOWER_TRICK.summary: Delayed area hit around the cast target. At cast time the strategy only records how many crits the cast target has received so far (its crit counter) and queues a command on the caster that runs 3000 ms later (on the first update after the delay has elapsed). When it runs it takes the difference between the target's crit counter now and at cast time (the counter does NOT count only successful crit hits; its semantics follow below) and takes the 3x3 block centred on the target's position AT THAT TIME (centre included) and gives every enemy unit in it SPECIAL damage of (raw 15/40/85 by the caster's stars + 15 per counted crit), AP-scaled and crit-multiplied only if the original cast crit. The crit bonus is added to the raw amount, so AP scaling applies to it too. The target is the unit fixed at cast time; it need not be alive or in the same cell, and the explosion is centred on its last known position. Nothing is dealt at cast time. Crit counter semantics: PokemonState.attack increments target.count.crit whenever a basic attack's crit roll succeeds, unless the target holds Rocky Helmet, BEFORE the dodge and protect checks, so a dodged or protected crit roll still counts although the attack dealt nothing. PokemonEntity.handleSpecialDamage increments it for a crit ability hit only after the protect / skydiving / magicBounce block, and Rocky Helmet suppresses it for non-TRUE damage only, so a TRUE ability crit still increments it. Pinned-helper probe: a forced crit that is dodged leaves basic damage 0 and raises the counter by 1, and a one-star Flower Trick then requests raw 30 instead of 15; with a Rocky Helmet, raw 10, AP 0 and critPower 2, a TRUE crit increments the counter and hands 20 to the damage handler while a SPECIAL crit leaves the counter at 0 and hands 10.

The counter rises (a) in PokemonState.attack whenever a basic attack's crit roll succeeds and the target has no Rocky Helmet, before the dodge and protect checks (so dodged or protected crit rolls count); (b) in PokemonEntity.handleSpecialDamage for a crit ability hit that passed the protect / skydiving / magicBounce block, except that Rocky Helmet suppresses it for non-TRUE damage only (a TRUE crit still counts). DARKEST_LARIAT.summary: Single-target multi-hit SPECIAL damage. The target is flinched for a requested 1000 ms, and round((1 + 0.01 x speed) x 3) hits (speed read at cast time) are queued as delayed commands at delays round(i x 1000 / hits) ms; each requests 1 x the caster's ATK (read at that hit; 2 x at 4 stars) as SPECIAL damage. Each callback tests the stored target's hp > 0 when it enters. Fire-synergy effects (WILDFIRE +1, BLAZE +2, DESOLATE_LAND +3, first match only) add attack to the caster AFTER the damage request of every callback that passed that hp test, even when the request was blocked (protect / skydiving / magicBounce, takenDamage 0) or dealt nothing, and even when it killed the target; a callback whose target already has hp 0 on entry makes neither request nor gain (pinned-strategy probe: WILDFIRE, ATK 30, blocked damage -> ATK 31 after the first callback). The caster then moves to the empty cell closest, by Manhattan distance and over the whole board, to the point target + (target - caster): the FULL vector from the caster to the target applied again from the target, not one sign-step past it; the point may lie off the board.

DRAGON_BREATH.summary: Directional breath. Deals flat SPECIAL damage (requested 25/50/100/200 by stars) to every enemy-team unit on the cells walked by effectInOrientation from the caster in one of 8 directions, limited to Chebyshev distance range + 1 = 2 from the caster. The direction is chosen by the sign of the target's offset (dx, dy), not an exact line to the target. Known helper exception: for RIGHT the loop is `x < board.rows` (6) although the production board has 8 columns and 6 rows, so the nominal two-cell ray is shortened: from a caster in column 3 or lower both cells are walked, from column 4 only column 5, from column 5 or beyond nothing. If no enemy is found on the walked cells (including when nothing is walked) the cast target itself is hit once by the helper's fallback; if an enemy was found, the fallback adds no extra hit (probe: caster (4,2), range 1, enemies (5,2) and (6,2), RIGHT -> only (5,2) receives a damage request).

RAGING_BULL.summary: Single-target ability. Damage lands on a shield first (whole amount unless flinched); a Protective Pads holder doubles the amount that hits a shield. The strategy does not read takenDamage, so applied damage does not feed back into the ability. A target with magicBounce also queues a 500-delayed SPECIAL bounce request aimed at the caster unless the caster holds Protective Pads (the bounce amount was not traced further).

AQUA_STEP.summary: The strategy computes a reference coordinate one sign-step from the caster toward the cast target (caster.x + sign(dx), caster.y + sign(dy)), asks board.getClosestAvailablePlace for the free cell closest (Manhattan) to that reference anywhere on the board, and requests a non-forced moveTo there. Because the search covers ALL free cells, the movement is not limited to one cell: it is the free cell nearest the reference, which can be far away on a crowded board (probe: caster (0,0), target (1,0), only free cell (7,5) -> move requested to (7,5)). With no free cell no move is requested. In every case a DelayedCommand with nominal delay 300 is queued; when it runs it requests SPECIAL damage on the cast target (raw 25/50/100/200 by stars) and adds speed to the caster (raw 10/15/20/25 by stars; AP-scaled). The 300 is a nominal delay consumed by update(dt) (the command runs on the first update that takes the delay below 0), not a guaranteed execution time.

lifecycle.freshAnnihilape: a newly created Annihilape (catalog instance, purchase, or the board unit produced by evolution) declares passive NONE, so a fight entity built from it has no PRIMEAPE effects and gains no stacks
lifecycle.existingEntityAfterMidFightEvolution: addStack changes only the existing entity's index, name and refToBoardPokemon (pokemon-entity.ts:1817-1822); it does not call changePassive. Read from the code: that entity keeps passive PRIMEAPE and its OnDeath/OnResurrecting effects for the rest of the fight, so a further death or resurrection would call addPrimeapeStack again: +1 ATK written permanently to the (now Annihilape) board unit and +1 on its stacks. The evolution rule re-check reads refToBoardPokemon.evolutionRule (Annihilape: not STACK), so no further evolution is attempted from addStack

conditions: Eviolite: StackEvolutionHandler.canEvolve returns false while it is held, and PokemonEntity.addStack calls tryEvolve only when stacks === stacksRequired, so on the addStack path an Eviolite holder that reaches 10 stacks does not evolve and stacks 11, 12, ... do not call tryEvolve again. This conclusion is limited to the inspected addStack path: other tryEvolve callers were not exhaustively listed, and canEvolve itself uses >=, so a different path that calls tryEvolve later could evolve it.
canEvolve also requires the unit to be on the player's board (stack-evolution-handler.ts:9).
A resurrection and the death that follows it each give a stack when they occur (two events), but a single hit that resurrects gives one (the death effect does not proc then).
PRIMEAPE.resetBehaviour: The stack count lives on the board Pokemon (refToBoardPokemon.stacks) and the permanent attack on its atk, so both persist across fights in the code read. No reset of stacks to 0 for Primeape was found (pattern search over `stacks = ` assignments in app/; not an exhaustive proof). The entity copy of stacks is taken from the board unit at fight start.
